title: Travel to court, before and after consolidation
description: The cost the reform paper asserts but cannot show, in three numbers per commune, all on the national road graph: to the court the law assigns it today, to the one court its county would keep, and to the nearest of the 42 wherever it sits. The third exists because a county line is a legal fact and not a geographic one — a Tulcea commune can be nearer to Braila — so the gap between the second and third is what the county rule costs on its own, apart from what consolidation costs.

workload.description: Dossiers per receiving court under each rule — the spread, not the list.

bucharestMultipleOfMean.description: How many times the average court Bucharest's own sectors amount to. They cannot be assigned elsewhere, so no ceiling below this is reachable by moving communes.

variation.description: Coefficient of variation of court loads — the honest measure here. Max-over-min is decided by whichever court ends up emptiest and moved the wrong way as the ceiling loosened.

metresToday.description: Road metres to the court the law assigns it. Null where the commune has no road to any court.

metresByCounty.description: Road metres to the one court its county would keep. Null where the commune has no road to any court.

metresNearest.description: Road metres to the nearest of the 42, ignoring county lines. Null where the commune has no road to any court.

nearestCounty.description: County of that nearest court. Differing from `county` means the commune would be served from another county if the boundary did not bind.

byRoad.description: False for the eleven communes with no road to any court, eight of them in the Danube Delta. They stay in the file and are excluded from every average.

cases.description: The commune's share of its court's dossiers, split by population, so that reassigning it moves work with it.

balancedMetres.description: Per-commune road metres under each load ceiling, aligned to `communes`. The key is the ceiling as a multiple of the average court; 99 means no ceiling at all, kept as a scenario so a control has one end of the trade to sit at.
